content:
[SUNDAY 26 JANUARY 1975 · 1975-01-26]
# SUNDAY 26 JANUARY 1975

Republic Day. We heard the parade on the radio and Arun
saluted every regiment from the sofa. Meera made a paper flag
and stuck it on the window.

New diary, new year. I promise to write every week this year.
title: SUNDAY 26 JANUARY 1975

content:
[SATURDAY 14 JUNE 1975 · 1975-06-14]
# SATURDAY 14 JUNE 1975

First real rain of the monsoon today. Arun and Meera ran out in
it before I could stop them, and came back laughing like two wet
puppies.

Mohan came home early with good news: he has been promoted
to Head Clerk from Ist July. 40 rupees more every month! !
made sheera for everyone. We will save the extra for Arun's
college.
title: SATURDAY 14 JUNE 1975

content:
[MONDAY 3 NOVEMBER 1975 · 1975-11-03]
# MONDAY 3 NOVEMBER 1975

Diwali week. Mohan saved from his Head Clerk raise to buy a
new pressure cooker for me and a mixer! Arun burnt a hole in his
shirt with a sparkler. Meera made the rangoli all by herself this
year.

Kheer for 14 people. Stirred for an hour.
title: MONDAY 3 NOVEMBER 1975

content:
[SATURDAY 25 JUNE 1983 · 1983-06-25]
# SATURDAY 25 JUNE 1983

India won the cricket World Cup! We watched the final on the
Shettys' television, the whole building squeezed into their hall.
When the last wicket fell Mohan and Arun jumped so high they
nearly hit the fan.

Meera went to bed at 2 am still waving the flag.
title: SATURDAY 25 JUNE 1983

content:
[SATURDAY 16 JULY 1983 · 1983-07-16]
# SATURDAY 16 JULY 1983

Arun left for Pune today on the Deccan Queen. Admission to
the College of Engineering, first list! Mohan pretended he had
dust in his eye at the station.

Packed: 2 bedsheets, his radio, ladoos, and the slide rule Mohan
used in the railway office.
title: SATURDAY 16 JULY 1983

content:
[SATURDAY 31 DECEMBER 1983 · 1983-12-31]
# SATURDAY 31 DECEMBER 1983

Last day of a big year. Arun home for the holidays, taller and
thinner. Meera topped her class in the Class X preliminary exam.
☒

We bought our own television on instalments, a black-and-white
Weston. The Shettys came to watch with us for a change.
title: SATURDAY 31 DECEMBER 1983

content:
[Meera's engagement today · 1991-09-10]
# TUESDAY 10 SEPTEMBER 1991

Meera's engagement today. Vikram Deshpande is a quiet, gentle
boy, a teacher at the same school where Meera teaches.
Wedding fixed for 8th December.

Mohan sang an old Mukesh song after dinner. Everyone
pretended it was good.
title: Meera's engagement today

content:
[Meera's wedding · 1991-12-08]
# SUNDAY 8 DECEMBER 1991

Meera's wedding. She wore my wedding saree, red with gold
border, from 1963. I made kheer for 200 guests with three
cooks and it was still the first dish to finish.

The house is very quiet tonight.
title: Meera's wedding

content:
[Railway Office, Jabalpur · 1962-04-04]
Railway Office, Jabalpur
4th April 1962

Respected Amma,

I have joined the Railway office here on
Monday, 2nd April, as a Junior clerk in the
accounts section. My salary will be RS 180
every month, and from the first salary I will
send you a new shawl .
title: Railway Office, Jabalpur

content:
[Railway Office, Jabalpur · 1962-04-04]
The Head Clerk, Shri verma, is strict but kind.
He checked my handwriting and said it is the
neatest in the office. I thought of Master Tiwari
from our school in sagar, who made us copy
whole pages until our letters stood straight. That
old school punishment has finally paid me a
salary !

I am staying with Ramesh in a rented room
near the station . Do not worry about food , his
mother feeds us both.

Your obedient son,

Mohan
title: Railway Office, Jabalpur

content:
[Letter from Kamla to Didi · 1964-11-20]
Dear Didi,

Our new house in Jabalpur is two rooms with a small
courtyard, and the neem tree outside gives shade all
afternoon. Mohan has planted tulsi near the door.

He works very hard in the railway office and comes home
only after seven. On Sundays we walk to the Bhedaghat
falls, it is so beautiful there.

Didi, I have some happy news which I will tell you properly
when you come for Holi. Do not tell Amma yet!

Your loving sister,
Kamla
title: Letter from Kamla to Didi

content:
[My dearest Kamla · 1965-08-10]
My dearest Kamla,

Your telegram reached us on Wednesday and the
whole house danced! A son! Amma distributed
laddoos to the whole lane. Arun is a lovely name,
strong and bright like the morning sun.

Rest properly for forty days and do not lift
anything heavy. I am sending you a parcel with
dry fruits, two small sweaters I knitted and
Amma's old silver bowl for the baby.
title: My dearest Kamla

content:
[My dearest Kamla · 1965-08-10]
I will come to Jabalpur in October to see my
nephew. Tell Mohan he must buy a camera now!

With love,
Savitri Didi
title: My dearest Kamla

content:
[Granddaughter has arrived · 1968-02-16]
Respected Amma ,

Your granddaughter has arrived! She was born
on wednesday the 14th, just before sunset, at
the railway hospital. Kamla is well and resting,
and the baby is small but very loud .

We have named her Meera , as you wished . Arun
keeps asking when she will be able to play
cricket .
title: Granddaughter has arrived

content:
[Granddaughter has arrived · 1968-02-16]
There is more news . Our whole office is being
transferred to Bombay next month. I will go
first with the office, and kamla and the
children will follow when the quarter is ready.

Your son,

Mohan
title: Granddaughter has arrived

content:
[Letter from Mohan to Kamla · 1968-03-09]
Goregaon , Bombay
9th March 1968

My dear Kamla,

we have shifted to Bombay. The whole office
came down by the Mail on Tuesday , files,
typewriters and all. The railway has given me a
small quarter in Goregaon, two rooms and a
kitchen, and the window looks at a coconut tree.

The sea is very big, Kamla. Yesterday evening !
walked from Dadar to the shore and stood there
Like a schoolboy. I thought of you and the
children the whole time.
title: Letter from Mohan to Kamla

content:
[Letter from Mohan to Kamla · 1968-03-09]
Give my love to Arun and kiss little Meera for
me. Ask Amma to write. I will send the train
fare on the first of the month, and by April you
will all be here.

Yours always,

Mohan
title: Letter from Mohan to Kamla

content:
[Diwali kheer note · 1971-10-28]
Dear Didi,

This Diwali I finally made the kheer the way Amma used to,
and Mohan took two helpings and asked for a third. I have
written it down on a card so it is not lost. I am keeping the
card in the trunk with our letters.

The secret is the old rice and the patience. Stir slowly, never
rush, just like Amma always said.

Arun has started school and Meera follows him everywhere.
Bombay is noisy but our neighbours are like family.

Your Kamla,

Kamla
title: Diwali kheer note

content:
[Letter from Mohan to Kamla · 1975-03-18]
Rail Bhavan, New Delhi
18th March 1975

Dear Kamla,

The meetings at the Railway Board end on
Friday and I will take the Frontier Mail back on
Saturday. Delhi is cold in the mornings and
very dusty .

My senior officer hinted that my name is on the
list for Head clerk. Do not tell anyone until it is
confirmed .

I bought a red cardigan for Meera and a cricket
bat for Arun from Karol Bagh . For you, a
surprise.

Yours,

Mohan
title: Letter from Mohan to Kamla

content:
[Usha's wedding · 1975-09-22]
Dear Kamla,

Usha's wedding is fixed! The boy is an engineer in
Bhopal, his family is simple and kind. The wedding
will be on 15th February 1976, so you must all
come for at least a week.

Congratulations to Mohan for becoming Head
Clerk. Amma says she always knew he would.

Please bring your kheer, nobody here makes it like
you.

Your Didi,
Savitri
title: Usha's wedding

content:
[Signed papers for Flat 6 in Shanti Niwas · 1979-11-15]
Respected Amma ,

Today we signed the papers and Flat 6 in
Shanti Niwas is now our own. We have lived
here as tenants since 1972 and now no
landlord can ask us to leave . Forty-eight
thousand rupees, Amma, all our savings and a
loan from the railway cooperative.

Kamla cried at the registrar's office and then
laughed at herself. Arun wants a bookshelf for
his engineering books and Meera wants a
window seat .

Please come and stay with us this winter . Your
room is ready .

Your son,

Mohan
title: Signed papers for Flat 6 in Shanti Niwas

content:
[Letter from Hostel 3, Pune · 1983-07-21]
Dear Papa and Aai,

I reached Pune safely. The College of Engineering is huge and
old, with stone buildings and a big ground. My room-mate is
Suresh from Nagpur, he snores but he is good at physics.

Classes start at eight. The mess food is not like Aai's, please
send some ladoos.

Papa, the lathe workshop is the best thing I have ever seen. I
think I want to build machines.

Your son,

Arun
title: Letter from Hostel 3, Pune

content:
[Meera writes to Dada about passing Twelfth and applying to teachers' training college · 1986-05-30]
Dada,

I passed my Twelfth with first class! Aai made shrikhand and
Papa told the whole building.

I have decided : I want to be a teacher. I have applied to the
teachers' training college in Dadar. Please tell Papa it is a good
job, he listens to you.

When are you coming home? Your bookshelf is now full of
my books.

Your sister,
Meera
title: Meera writes to Dada about passing Twelfth and applying to teachers' training college

content:
[Letter to Arun about his new job · 1990-06-12]
Goregaon , Bombay
12th June 1990

Dear Arun,

Your letter about the new job made your mother
cry and your father very proud . Design
engineer at a machine tools company, with a
salary three times what I earned when I started !
Do your work honestly and the rest will follow .

I have three more years before I retire from the
railway . Your mother wants to visit indore and
see the sea in Goa, in that order.

come home for Ganpati. Bring your friend
Anjali if she can come.

Your papa,

Mohan
title: Letter to Arun about his new job

[Dal Tadka · 1966]
# Dal Tadka

1966

\- 1 cup toor dal

\- salt to taste

\- I tomato, chopped

\- 2 tbsp ghee

\- 1 tsp turmeric

\- 1 tsp cumin, 4 garlic, 2 red chillies
Pressure-cook dal with turmeric and salt (3 whistles). Mash, add tomato, simmer.
Heat ghee, crackle cumin, garlic and chillies, pour over the dal.

Mohan's favourite on Mondays
title: Dal Tadka

content:
[Kheer (the real one) · 1971]
# Kheer (the real one)

\- 1 litre full-cream milk
\- 4 green cardamom, crushed

\- 1/4 cup old rice, washed
\- 1/2 cup sugar

\- a pinch of saffron in warm milk
\- 10 almonds, sliced

Boil the milk, add rice, keep the flame low. Stir slowly, never rush. When it coats the
spoon (about 45 minutes) add sugar, cardamom and saffron. Almonds on top.
Stir slowly, never rush! - K.
title: Kheer (the real one)

content:
[Besan Ladoo · 1974]
1974

# Besan Ladoo

\- 2 cups besan

\- 1/2 tsp cardamom

\- 3/4 cup ghee

\- chopped cashews

\- 1 cup powdered sugar

Roast besan in ghee on low heat for 25 minutes till it smells nutty. Cool a little, mix
sugar, cardamom and cashews, shape while warm.

Do not burn the besan!
title: Besan Ladoo

content:
[Aloo Paratha · 1969]
# Aloo Paratha

1969

\- 2 cups wheat flour

\- coriander leaves

\- 3 boiled potatoes
\- ajwain, salt
\- ghee for roasting

\- I green chilli

Knead a soft dough. Mash potatoes with chilli, coriander, ajwain and salt. Fill, roll
gently, roast with ghee on both sides till golden spots appear.

Arun eats three!
title: Aloo Paratha

content:
[Mango Pickle (Amma style) · 1982-05]
# Mango Pickle (Amma style)

May 1982

\- 2 kg raw mangoes
\- red chilli powder

\- 1 cup mustard oil
\- turmeric, salt
\- mustard and fenugreek seeds
\- a pinch of hing
Cut mangoes, dry in the sun for a day. Mix spices, add mangoes and warm oil. Keep
in the sun for a week, shake the jar every morning.

Dry jar only!
title: Mango Pickle (Amma style)

content:
[Kanda Poha · 1978]
1978

# Kanda Poha

\- 2 cups thick poha

\- mustard seeds, curry leaves

\- / onion

\- turmeric, salt, sugar

\- lemon and coriander

\- peanuts

Rinse poha and drain. Fry peanuts, mustard, curry leaves and onion, add turmeric,
then poha, salt and a pinch of sugar. Lemon and coriander on top.

Meera's Sunday breakfast
title: Kanda Poha
